newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA BRIEFING - MAY.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA BRIEFING - MAY.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HAMBURG - Advertising executive Willi Schalk has criticised the regulations of the German television market. Because commercial breaks are so lengthy, viewers are developing hostility toward TV ads, he says in the latest issues of news magazine Der Spiegel. The problem breeds channel surfing during commercial pauses because the ad blocks are too spread apart and too long. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Money spent on sponsorship will increase to 3.2 billion marks ($1.9 billion) in the year 2000, a jump from the current level of 2.8 billion marks. Sports are predicted to remain the main beneficiaries of sponsorship in Germany. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Publicis sold its 50 percent share in the convention company Publicis MCD Messe GmbH to electronics group Siemens, which will manage the company's business alone in the future. (Horizont)
DUESSELDORF - Advertising agency TBWA says its Frankfurt office has won the multimillion mark account of video game unit Sony Playstation and plans to fight off chief competitor Nintendo. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Lowe & Partners says it will begin running the campaign of Moevenpick FeinJoghurt. The Frankfurt-based agency says it will start a television campaign for the yogurt in the autumn of this year. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Television broadcaster ProSieben, which plans this summer to become the first German TV station with a stock market listing, expects sizeable interest in its initial public offering, ProSieben chairman Georg Kofler says in the German weekly Focus magazine. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG plans to steer its cable business into the black with price increases and programming package marketing, Der Spiegel reports. In the last year alone, Telekom posted 500 million marks in losses from a 17 million mark budget, Der Spiegel says. (Reuter)

MUNICH - The fourth largest private German television station, RTL2, is planning personnel changes, Luxembourg-based broadcasting company CLT-Ufa says. The company says current RTL2 chairman Rudolf-Markus Reischl will not extend his contract beyond June 30. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The national association of German newspaper publishers (BDZV) says Bild Online topped the ranks of Internet web sites with almost three million PageViews and nearly 400,000 visits. (Horizont)

MUNICH - Children are watching more and more television, but are viewing less programming aimed at children, according to study by private broadcaster ZDF. Viewing times increased last year among three to 13 year olds by six minutes to 101 minutes per day, ZDF says. (Focus)
HAMBURG - German cinemagoers are supporting more German productions. Even successful foreign films like The English Patient and Evita are only ranked ninth and nineteenth respectively. (Der Spiegel)

MUNICH - Private channel Super RTL has higher ratings among children than public stations ARD or ZDF or private broadcaster Sat1 with a more than 12 percent market share among children. The channel tops the other stations although it is only available in two-thirds of German households. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
HAMBURG - Cologne-based private channel RTL plans to launch a weekly erotic programme. (Focus)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
FRANKFURT - Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG soar in otherwise lacklustre early dealing on Monday amid positive sentiment ahead of its annual news conference on Tuesday. (Reuter)
STUTTGART - Plant construction group Duerr AG says it has won an order worth more than 300 million marks to build a paintworks for Daimler-Benz AG. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Beverage and bottling machinery maker Krones AG names Lorenz Raith as new head of its supervisory board. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Richard Roy will become chairman of software maker Microsoft's German unit in Unterschleissheim. Roy comes from Siemens Nixdorf (SNI). (Horizont)
MUNICH - ProSieben names newscaster Wolfgang Klein as director of its news editorial division. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - Stephan Becker-Sonnenschein has been made president of the German Public Relations Association (DPRG). Becker-Sonnenschein is the manager of PR marketing at Philip Morris in Munich. (Kress)
